explain.say: The people we call Byzantines never used that word. They called themselves Romans, and their empire lasted until 1453, almost a thousand years after the West fell. A German scholar, Hieronymus Wolf, made the name Byzantine popular in 1557. Look at the timeline of this long survival.

explain.say: Look at the second and third dots. Justinian, emperor from 527 to 565, gathered centuries of Roman law into one great collection that still shapes legal systems in Europe and beyond. He also built Hagia Sophia, finished in 537, under a dome that seemed to float. Why would a ruler collect old laws?

explain.say: Justinian also tried to win back the West. Look at the map: his generals retook North Africa from the Vandals, with Carthage, and Italy with Rome, after long wars. But in 541 a terrible plague struck. Why might reconquest and plague together exhaust an empire?

Then came hard centuries: Arab armies took Syria and Egypt in the 630s and 640s, and the Seljuk Turks won at Manzikert in 1071. Yet the empire survived, thanks to strong city walls, gold coins, skilled diplomacy and Greek fire, a burning liquid used at sea. Which do you think mattered most?

explain.say: In 1453 the Ottoman sultan Mehmed II took Constantinople. Edward Gibbon saw only decline, but historians like Judith Herrin and Anthony Kaldellis show a resilient, inventive Roman state. See the debate. Great work. Exam tip: say Eastern Roman Empire at least once, to show you know the name is modern.

faq.a: The eastern half of the Roman Empire, ruled from Constantinople, which survived after the West fell in the fifth century and lasted until 1453. Its people called themselves Romans; the name Byzantine was popularised by later scholars.
asks: What is the Eastern Roman Empire?

faq.q: Why did the Byzantine Empire last so long?
faq.a: Strong walls around Constantinople, a professional administration and tax system, a trusted gold coin, clever diplomacy and military technology such as Greek fire helped it survive many crises.
asks: How did Constantinople survive so many sieges?

faq.a: Justinian, who ruled 527 to 565, collected Roman law into the Corpus Juris Civilis, built Hagia Sophia, and reconquered North Africa and Italy, though these wars and the plague of 541 strained the empire.
asks: What is the Corpus Juris Civilis?

faq.a: A dispute from 726 to 843, with breaks, over whether religious images, icons, should be venerated. Iconoclast emperors removed or destroyed images; in 843 icon veneration was restored.

faq.q: When and how did Constantinople fall?
faq.a: On 29 May 1453, after a siege of about seven weeks, Ottoman forces under Sultan Mehmed II broke through the walls, using huge cannon. The last emperor, Constantine XI, died in the fighting.

facts: Constantinople was dedicated as the new capital in 330.
Hagia Sophia was completed in 537 under Justinian.
Constantinople fell to the Ottomans on 29 May 1453.

quiz.say: What did the Byzantines call themselves?
quiz.why: They called themselves Romaioi, Romans; Byzantine is a later scholars' label.

wrong.1: That name was popularised by Hieronymus Wolf in 1557.
wrong.2: They spoke Greek but saw themselves as Romans.

quiz.say: Which event of 1204 badly weakened the empire?
quiz.why: Crusaders looted the city and set up a Latin empire until 1261.

wrong.2: Justinian's code was compiled in 529 to 534.
